speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with painful urination, and you have a history of a similar episode in your left ankle. To help me diagnose your condition, have you noticed any stiffness in your morning hours, and does the pain improve with movement or rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome). The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, ankle), urethritis, and risk factors for sexually transmitted infections in a young male is highly suggestive, so I will now request a Urine_Culture, Chlamydia_DNA, and HLA-B27 test to confirm the etiology and rule out septic arthritis.
